newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp steel workers demand job guarantee.
newsitem.headline: Krupp steel workers demand job guarantee.

text.p: The 6,000 steel workers employed by the Krupp group in Dortmund said on Tuesday they would not return to work until they are guaranteed that no new job losses would arise from a steel venture with Thyssen.

The steel workers, employed by Krupp Hoesch Stahl, had been protesting over thousands of job losses they fear would have resulted from a takeover by parent company Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp of Thyssen AG.
Krupp on Monday called off its 13.6 billion marks ($8.1 billion) hostile bid and both sides said they would form a steel joint venture and explore other potential areas for cooperation.
Krupp's steel production facilities are less modern than Thyssen's, and the workforce fears that it could be the first to face job losses under a new venture controlled by Thyssen.
Works council member Bernd Schimmeyer said workers demanded that the 2,200 job losses at the Dortmund works foreseen under a cost-cutting plan announced in February not be exceeded.
